headline: Washington's Chip Leverage and AI's Missing Independent Evidence
paragraphs: The most consequential item today is not a product. Internal notes from an August 2025 call, described in a federal lawsuit, record Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro telling Intel's chief financial officer that a roughly 10 percent US government equity stake was not up for bargaining: "Do not make the mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation." According to a summary of his remarks prepared for Intel's directors, he acknowledged the board could decline, but said rejection "will have consequences that [he] cannot predict." The same day brought the MATCH Act — proposed, not enacted — which would bar ASML from servicing the roughly 350 immersion DUV scanners already installed in China; a LithoWar analysis argues a service cutoff would backfire, pushing maintenance to rival firms, inviting reverse engineering and letting competitors recruit ASML-trained staff. Both stories treat the chip supply chain as an instrument of leverage whose side effects nobody has modeled.

Below the policy fight, the hardware stack is diversifying at both ends. SemiAnalysis's Trainium3 deep dive places AWS's accelerator on its InferenceX leaderboard with a better throughput-per-TCO frontier than every listed part except Nvidia's Vera Rubin, and says it trades blows with or beats GB300 on cost to generate tokens — crediting design choices rather than Amazon's supply position. That is a benchmarking firm's leaderboard, not an audited result. Kioxia, meanwhile, showed a third-generation XL-Flash prototype it says reaches 3 µs average read latency against 40 µs for its BiCS8 TLC, at 70% higher bit density, aimed at the tier between DRAM and conventional flash that Intel's Optane once targeted. Samples arrive in March 2027.

The AI announcements share a different problem: the evidence mostly comes from the claimant. Google Research's DeepCrossAttention, which lets each token attend to embeddings from prior layers, reports comparable quality with up to 3x faster performance — Google's own lab claims, with no independent benchmark or peer-reviewed paper in the reporting. DeepMind's "Humanity's First Exam" tested 18 models: top performers solved nearly every task family at least once but failed to give 16 correct answers in a row, with GPT-6.2 Astra the strongest and still inconsistent, visual perception behind 73% of the errors, and extra inference compute not closing the gap — DeepMind's own evaluation again. Embo emerged from stealth with a $110 million seed led by a16z for world-model robot AI trained on internet video and simulation, with researchers from DeepMind, Meta and MIT, but no product, benchmark, customer or timeline. The check that exists, repeatability, is the one the models fail.

Electrification is arriving in measurable but unevenly documented ways. Fraunhofer's Energy-Charts put German solar past 100 TWh in a calendar year for the first time — 100.2 TWh by the morning of Nov. 27, about 10 TWh above the 90 TWh recorded for 2025, with 16.9 TWh consumed on site, and solar the second-largest source of net generation behind wind. The EV headline is softer: InsideEVs reported that EVs outsold petrol and diesel combined in the EU in October, turning a 127,000-car deficit into a lead of nearly 70,000, but gave no totals, no market-share percentages and no definition of whether "EV" includes plug-in hybrids. The hardware is announced but unquantified: CATL's 100 kWh "30#" swappable pack with a sub-minute swap, which are company claims with no chemistry, models, date or price disclosed; Toyota's Highlander 9X EREV due early 2027 on Huawei and CATL technology, with no range, battery size or markets given; and the BRF Froan's 23.5 MWh battery, where "largest" is the outlet's characterization rather than a verified record.

Two contradictions sit underneath. The trust layer is soft: SAP confirmed suspicious activity on GitHub, while the claim that stolen employee tokens let attackers copy and alter source code rests on SecurityWeek's reporting — SAP has not said which repositories, how many accounts, or whether altered code reached shipped software. TU Berlin researchers separately showed AMD fTPM and Winbond SPI flaws that let an attacker with physical access defeat BitLocker's failed-attempt lockout and brute-force a short PIN faster. And timelines stay long: Stoke Space's Nova Pathfinder reached pad SLC-14 on Nov. 22 after a 17-day road trip, the first rocket there since the 1960s, but a wet dress rehearsal campaign, engine integration, a static fire and second-stage mating still precede an early-2027 launch. Watch whether the Intel stake closes and on what terms, whether the MATCH Act advances as drafted, and whether anyone independently replicates DeepMind's exam.
takeaways: The US government is treating an Intel equity stake as leverage rather than a negotiation, and export policy toward ASML carries similarly unmodeled risk.
Most of today's AI performance claims, from DeepCrossAttention to Humanity's First Exam to Embo, come from the organizations making them without independent benchmarks.
Electrification is spreading into bulk shipping, buses and extended-range vehicles, but October's EU EV crossover and several battery claims lack the data to verify them.
